metadata.case_name: KAN KWOK CHEUNG v. CHEUNG CHUNG T/A 實惠室內裝修傢俬設計公司

plaintiff.occupation_before: Kitchen worker, cleaning worker, gardener, construction site worker and mason worker; night shift security guard; casual courier and part-time furniture/miscellaneous worker

injuries.description: Permanent blindness of the left eye following severe bacterial infection and left eye evisceration
source: the Plaintiff received surgery on 24 October 2006 for removal of his left eye eyeball content (ie left eye evisceration) as a result of serious bacterial infection. An ocular medpor implant was inserted at the time as a volume replacement.
His visual acuity was 20/100 for right eye and permanent blindness for the left.

injuries.description: Left eye socket and left eyelid scarring with sunken left eye socket and inability to wear artificial eye (disfiguring/cosmetic appearance)
source: Due to the numerous operations after the Accident, the Plaintiff’s left eye socket and left eyelid had many scars, and he could no longer wear any artificial eye. He could not accept his cosmetic appearance following loss of his left eye with sunken left eye socket and dark eyelid that were full of scars and wrinkles.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

injuries.description: Large left corneal ulcer with infiltrate; bacterial culture yielded pseudomonas species (infective corneal ulcer)
source: large left eye cornea ulcer around 6mm with infiltrate
bacterial culture of the ulcer yielded pseudomonas species.

injuries.description: Pre-existing bilateral glaucoma with poor vision in left and impaired right eye plus cataract of right eye
source: The Plaintiff suffered from bilateral glaucoma with visual acuity in the left eye being light perception to hand movement whilst that of the right eye was 0.1 to 0.2 (ie about 50%).
The Plaintiff's right eye vision was also abnormal. He had history of glaucoma in 2005, and the present vision was only 0.1 due to glaucoma and significant cataract over his right eye.

injuries.description: Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (psychiatric injury)
source: the Plaintiff had been suffering from an adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood that was a reaction to the stresses at the time of the Accident, the physical impairment after the Accident, and the social consequences such as the employment and financial problems.

manifestations.description: Total loss of vision of the left eye
Poor/reduced vision of the right eye (e.g. 20/100; 0.1 to 0.2)
Sunken left eye socket and scarred/dark left eyelid (disfiguring appearance)
Pain in the left eye following the Accident
Depressive mood, sleep disturbances, reduced appetite, irritability, impaired sexual desire, reduced interest and social interactions, mild impairment of concentration and frequent worries
Avoidance behaviour, emotional numbness and reduced interest (PTSD-like symptoms but not meeting PTSD diagnostic criteria)
Loss of ability to engage in pre-Accident sports and hobbies (playing football and basketball, swimming, picnicking and singing karaoke)

treatments_received: Admission to NDH AED and initial eyedrops/painkillers (7 October 2006 and 9 October 2006)
Admission to AHMLNH and intensive antibiotics (admitted 9 October 2006)
Admission to PWH DOVS and surgery: left eye evisceration with ocular medpor implant insertion (24 October 2006)
Repair of left conjunctival wound, revision of left orbital implant, and lid reconstruction (4 March 2008)
Reconstruction of left eyelid with tarsoconjunctival flap and orbital reconstruction for orbital implant exposure (8 April 2008)
Reconstruction of left eyelid with tarsoconjunctival flap (18 June 2008)
Removal of left orbital implant (26 September 2008)
Right eye cataract extraction and intraocular lens implantation (23 April 2009)
Ongoing ophthalmic follow up at AHMLNH and PWH (multiple sessions)
Occupational therapy (from 16 December 2006; about 8 sessions between Dec 2008 and Feb 2009)
Psychiatric treatment and medication (first presented 22 May 2008; about 15 sessions from 22 May 2008 to 23 February 2010)
treatments_future: Further surgeries planned by PWH to try to improve facial appearance (Liang Report)
Ongoing ophthalmic and psychiatric follow up; possible private-sector psychiatric and clinical psychological treatment if public sector insufficient

losses.description: Total loss of vision of the left eye (permanent blindness) following evisceration
Sunken left eye socket, dark eyelid full of scars and wrinkles and inability to wear artificial eye; cosmetically unacceptable appearance

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Gave up pre-Accident sports and hobbies including playing football and basketball, swimming, picnicking and singing karaoke

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Stayed at home and did not want to go out; wore sunglasses when going out; feared discrimination by others

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Impaired sexual desire as part of psychiatric consequences
Unable to engage in any gainful employment after the Accident; unsuccessful job applications due to eye problem and disfigurement

the Plaintiff had been suffering from an adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood that was a reaction to the stresses at the time of the Accident, the physical impairment after the Accident, and the social consequences such as the employment and financial problems.
